facts.title: Texas BEAD final proposal — current approved program snapshot
facts.value: 22 selected applicants; >240,000 BSLs; >2,700 CAIs; $1.2B federal grant funding + $177M state match
facts.note: BDO says projects were expected to begin construction as soon as summer 2026. Treat award, construction and operational status separately.

facts.title: Texas BEAD technology mix in NTIA overview
facts.value: 242,903 eligible locations: 122,994 FTTP (50.6%); 65,901 LEO satellite (27.1%); 54,008 fixed wireless (22.3%)
facts.note: NTIA overview says data were based on Final Proposal submissions and subject to curing/NIST review at publication.

facts.title: BOOT I and II infrastructure awards
facts.value: BOOT I: $10.4M for 1,468 residences, 77 businesses, 15 CAIs. BOOT II: $623.4M for 61,185 residences, 18,250 businesses, 2,191 CAIs.
facts.note: BOOT I projects must be completed by Dec. 31, 2026; BOOT II has project-specific deadlines and monthly status files.

facts.title: Technical Assistance Program county planning
facts.value: 32 counties accepted for direct broadband planning and consulting assistance
facts.note: The BDO page lists participating counties and whether county broadband plan services are complete or being finalized.

facts.title: Building the Texas Broadband Workforce Grant Program
facts.value: $24.6M; 7 grantees; projected 2,800 Texans trained in fiber installation, maintenance and repair
facts.note: Programs support tuition-free industry-recognized credentials, micro-credentials, degrees and work-based learning.

facts.title: Texas Broadband Pole Replacement Program
facts.value: Two reimbursement rounds awarded $18.5M and $9.8M; program page reports $46.7M fund balance for future NOFAs
facts.note: Eligible reimbursements are subject to program rules; future NOFAs should be verified at the official page before planning around them.

facts.title: Texas FY2026 E-Rate State Match Fund
facts.value: Up to $5,000,000 in state match funding for eligible school-system E-Rate projects
facts.note: TEA also posts current E-Rate implementation notices and state-match eligibility requirements.

facts.title: Healthcare Connect Fund
facts.value: 65% discount on eligible broadband connectivity expenses for eligible rural health care providers
facts.note: Eligibility and competitive-bidding requirements apply. FY2027 request-for-services activity began July 1, 2026.

facts.title: FCC National Broadband Map scope
facts.value: Shows provider-reported availability; does not by itself measure performance, affordability or adoption
facts.note: Users can submit availability challenges when map information appears inaccurate.

facts.title: Texas Broadband Development Map definition
facts.value: Texas map defines broadband service for the state map as at least 100/20 Mbps with latency of 100 ms or less using specified reliable technologies
facts.note: BDO states its map uses FCC Broadband Data Collection data and links to BEAD award mapping and challenge guidance.

facts.title: Texas library broadband role
facts.value: TSLAC treats public-library broadband as infrastructure for workforce, education/training and health access and recommends the Toward Gigabit Libraries Toolkit
facts.publisher: Texas State Library and Archives Commission
facts.note: Libraries can also use E-Rate and TSLAC digital-opportunity resources.

facts.title: Libraries Improving, Funding, Infrastructure (LIFI) / CPF work
facts.value: 2025 performance report described 37 libraries expected to serve more than 1 million Texans through broadband/digital-access infrastructure work
facts.note: Use as a dated program-performance reference; verify current completion status before describing a site as operational.

facts.title: Texas Digital Opportunity Plan
facts.value: Accepted March 28, 2024; BDO says infrastructure alone is insufficient and identifies affordability, devices, digital skills and cybersecurity as core conditions
facts.note: BDO states State Digital Equity Capacity Grant funding was terminated and it is seeking alternative avenues while continuing TDOP goals.

facts.title: Census digital-access measurement tables
facts.value: ACS tables S2801/B28002/B28003 provide household computer and internet-subscription measures; latest source surfaced here is 2024 ACS
facts.note: Use Census geographies and margins of error when comparing counties/tracts; do not equate subscription with service quality.

facts.title: Texas public-sector digital accessibility
facts.value: Texas DIR identifies state/local government, public education, public hospitals/clinics, libraries, transit and other public entities as subject to digital-accessibility requirements
facts.note: The OS targets WCAG 2.2 AA as a design goal; regulated entities should consult current legal/agency requirements.

facts.title: Texas emergency-warning continuity emphasis
facts.value: TDEM's April 2026 statewide drill asked local alerting authorities to exercise primary, alternate and contingency warning systems
facts.note: Useful planning precedent for resilient communications; this OS does not replace official alerting systems.

facts.title: Texas Small Business Resource Portal
facts.value: State portal produces customized resource lists for starting or growing a business, including funding, licensing/permitting, training and local resources
facts.publisher: Office of the Texas Governor — Economic Development & Tourism
facts.note: Users should review the portal privacy/public-disclosure notice before submitting information.

facts.title: Texas State Training Inventory
facts.value: TWC inventory supports searching education and workforce training providers/programs by region, ZIP and field of study
facts.note: Useful for connecting broadband workforce or digital-skills plans to actual training supply.

facts.title: DIR TEX-AN and public-sector connectivity procurement
facts.value: DIR describes TEX-AN as competitively procured voice, data and internet connectivity services for eligible public-sector organizations
facts.note: Eligibility and contract terms must be checked with DIR.

programs.name: Texas BEAD
programs.action: Inspect award map and project files; distinguish award, construction, activation and adoption.

programs.name: BOOT I / II
programs.action: Use monthly awardee status files; BOOT I completion deadline is Dec. 31, 2026.

programs.name: Technical Assistance Program
programs.action: Review county broadband plans and data where published.

programs.name: Texas Broadband Pole Replacement
programs.status: Prior rounds awarded; future NOFAs TBD
programs.who: Eligible pole owners / broadband service providers
programs.action: Do not assume a new round is open; verify official page.

programs.name: Building the Texas Broadband Workforce
programs.action: Use grantee/program details to route trainees to tuition-free fiber pathways when available.

programs.name: E-Rate / Texas State Match
programs.status: FY2026 filing window closed; program continues by funding year
programs.action: Use current USAC and TEA funding-year guidance; do not reuse closed deadlines.

programs.name: Healthcare Connect Fund
programs.who: Eligible rural health care providers / consortia
programs.action: Check site eligibility, competitive bidding and current funding-year deadlines in RHC Connect.

programs.name: Texas Digital Opportunity Plan / Hub
programs.action: Use plan/barrier framework and current BDO mapping resources; verify any grant opportunity separately.
